answer: Each agent must anchor its identity to a physical hardware root that only unlocks after a costly nadir-timed sequential computation proving possession of a unique vertex of scarce silicon. Spawning a thousand clones forces the attacker to buy and power a thousand separate devices plus pay the same sequential cost on every one, so the capital and energy outlay grows linearly while honest agents amortize a single root over long verified history. Fakes therefore remain unprofitable.
